source_read: PDF, pp. 728-736 (all pages; Tables 1 and 2 and the Comment checked on pages rendered at 110 dpi). Step 1 (blind extraction) not run this round, per the round brief.

design.note: Prospective cohort within the Netherlands XTC Toxicity study, with testing before any use; the card's statement of what it can and cannot establish matches the paper.

key_findings.note: Checked p. 731, 1st paragraph of Neuropsychological Testing: F(12, 96) = 0.73, p = .72, partial eta squared 0.08. Worth one word of care in any claim built on it: this is a single multivariate test, not 12 separate ones.
Checked text p. 731 and Table 2 on the rendered p. 732; every figure matches.
Checked text p. 731 and Table 2; every figure matches.

Checked Table 2, its footnotes and the text on p. 732. Recomputed the editors' note: 22.4% of 58 is 13 people, 6.7% of 60 is 4, crude odds ratio 4.04. The adjusted odds ratio 5.87 and Wald chi-square 5.62 are in the text.
Checked Table 2: the nine other rows run from p = .21 to p = .85, and the text states no sex by ecstasy interaction.
Checked p. 732, 3rd paragraph. Recomputed the editors' arithmetic: 15 of 58 and 3 of 60 were excluded.
Checked p. 732. Recomputed the editors' note: for r = -0.24, n = 58, two-tailed p = .070; for r = -0.29, two-tailed p = .027. Both agree.

Checked Comment 2nd paragraph (p. 732-733) and 6th paragraph (p. 733-734); each item listed is there.

reporting_issues.note: Table 1, p. 731: duration 6.8 (SD 12.5) weeks with median 0.0 and range 0 to 12. Recomputed: with a median of 0 and a maximum of 12 the mean cannot exceed 6.0 and the SD cannot exceed 6, so the row is impossible as printed.
Table 2, p. 732. Recomputed: ln(5.87) = 1.770, and the logarithms of 1.36 and 25.37 (0.31 and 3.23) centre on 1.77, so the printed B is on the log-odds scale and the interval on the odds-ratio scale.

Table 2, p. 732: the comparison group's means fall 3.4 to 3.1 with a change printed as +0.10, and rise 20.8 to 20.9 with a change printed as -0.33; with score SDs of 0.5 and 0.3 a change SD of 1.8 is impossible.
Checked the abstract (p. 728), Methods (p. 729) and Table 1 (p. 731): matched on sex, age and verbal IQ; other substance use adjusted for, not matched, and higher in the ecstasy group.

Checked the title and abstract against the sensitivity analysis (p. 732) and Table 1: 15 of 58 had used cocaine or amphetamines, with an amphetamine range to 156 times in the ecstasy group at follow-up.
Checked the abstract (p. 728) and Table 2: immediate recall rose from 58.7 to 59.6 in the ecstasy group, so for that measure the finding is a smaller gain, not a decline.

instrument.note: ROBINS-E, correct for a non-randomized follow-up study of an exposure.

domains.note: Some concerns is right: baseline scores were equal and adjusted for, but cannabis and cocaine use rose more in the ecstasy group and sensation seeking was measured only in the wider cohort.
The 8-month difference in retest interval on a repeated word list is the most important item here, and the card names it.

overall.note: High. No single domain is high, so this is an escalation from six domains at some concerns, which ROBINS-E allows and which I think the facts justify: the finding is a difference in practice gain, measured at intervals that differ by 8 months, in groups that differ in cannabis and cocaine use. A reader who left the overall at some concerns would not be unreasonable, so I record this as agreement with the reasoning rather than a close call hidden behind a word.

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial. The abstract's 'decline in verbal memory' is a smaller gain for immediate recall, and the abstract's statement that the groups were matched on use of other substances is contradicted by the Methods and Table 1. The abstract does carry the normal-range caveat, which the card records.

missed: Methods, p. 729: the same participants also underwent brain imaging, 'analyzed and described by other investigators in separate articles'. This is the paper's own evidence that the imaging cohort published as de Win et al. (2008) is this same 188-person sample, which settles the point AI reader 25 raised about Parrott (2013) presenting them as two cohorts. Worth adding to this card, because the editor will look for it here.

The dose-response odds ratio for recognition decline with log-transformed tablets, 15.18, has a 95% interval of 1.10 to 210.14 (p. 732): the card reports it but does not say that an interval spanning two orders of magnitude cannot carry a dose-response claim. The claim text should never quote that odds ratio without its interval.

p. 734: the authors argue from the brain-reserve hypothesis that their well-educated sample may have led them to underestimate the effect. This is a limitation that runs against their own result's direction and belongs beside the ones the card lists, for balance.

p. 734: the authors support the exposure measure with Dutch pill-testing data (95% of tablets sold as ecstasy in 2003 and 2004 contained MDMA as the major component). The card's exposure field records the absence of purity testing but not this partial answer to it.
